subject: Liability redlines: materiality and fraud/gross-negligence thresholds (Neptune)
messages:
From: Oliver Gray <oliver.gray@neptune.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Katy Simmons <katy.simmons@neptune.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T08:12:00Z
Subject: Neptune redlines on MSA (liability section)

Jonas — attaching our redline to the MSA and the Order Form. We've highlighted three areas we need to preserve: (1) broad carve-out for fraud and willful misconduct, (2) a materiality threshold for triggering certain remedies, and (3) removal of consequential damages carve-outs that would swallow other protections.

Key ask: please confirm you can accept an uncapped carve-out for proven intentional fraud and willful misconduct; otherwise we won't be able to accept a token cap for those categories. We included comments in the doc where we think definitions can be tightened.

Attachments: Neptune_MSA_Redline_20261008.docx (track changes), Neptune_OrderForm_v3.pdf

Thanks — look forward to getting your legal team's view.

--
Oliver Gray
Head of Legal, Neptune Analytics
oliver.gray@neptune.com

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Gray <oliver.gray@neptune.com>
Cc: Katy Simmons <katy.simmons@neptune.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-08T12:05:00Z
Subject: RE: Neptune redlines on MSA (liability section)

Oliver / Katy — thanks for the redlines and the clear callouts. I've looped in our legal and engineering leads for a quick run-through. High level: we can accept carve-outs for proven fraud and willful misconduct, but we need (i) a narrowly tailored definition of "willful misconduct" and (ii) objective thresholds around what constitutes a "material" breach for certain remedies to kick in (and to avoid trivial disputes later).

Proposed from our side (draft, subject to legal):
- Fraud / intentional wrongdoing: uncapped liability, but limited to acts proven by clear and convincing evidence.
- Willful misconduct: carve-out only where there is intentional or deliberate action taken with knowledge of substantial likelihood of harm; reckless omissions should be treated differently and tied to a monetary/materiality floor.
- Materiality trigger: suggest a bright-line of either $250,000 in direct damages or a continuous production outage of 48+ hours.

Laura / Stephanie / Dev — can you confirm whether these are workable? Also, Dev — can you confirm what trace evidence we can provide (logs, audit trails, SSO events) to support intent findings?

Jonas
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-08T15:30:00Z
Subject: RE: Neptune redlines on MSA (liability section)

Quick read-through: I like the direction. A few concrete edits we should propose back (so I can draft language):
1) Define "willful misconduct" as "intentional wrongdoing or deliberate action taken with knowledge that the conduct is substantially certain to cause harm." That keeps out negligence and borderline reckless acts.
2) For "reckless" behavior we can allow a separate carve-out only where the conduct is shown by a preponderance of the evidence AND the claimant can show either (a) >$500k direct damages or (b) a quantifiable security breach (data exfiltration affecting >10k records). This prevents fishing expeditions.
3) Material breach: recommend either $250k OR three separate incidents within a rolling 90-day window causing measurable customer impact; that avoids single-ticket escalations turning into contract-wide remedies.
4) Caps language: our standard approach is the greater of $5M or 2x the annual fees paid in the prior 12 months for aggregate liability (excluding uncapped fraud/willful misconduct). We can be flexible on the dollar floor for strategic accounts.

I will prepare a tracked-redline response tonight and propose we aim to get Neptune to agree on definitions first — caps can be negotiated after.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-09T09:08:00Z
Subject: RE: Neptune redlines on MSA (liability section)

Laura / team — on the evidence front, here's what we can provide to support claims of intent/recklessness:
- Immutable audit logs for admin API calls (retained 365 days) with timestamps and source IPs.
- Model inference logs (token-level provenance) for 90 days behind access controls.
- SSO/SCIM change history and role assignments.
- We can also provide a certified export and attestation if legal needs an evidentiary packet, but that takes 5-7 business days to compile.

From a risk perspective, tying the "reckless" standard to a clear evidentiary bar plus a monetary threshold makes sense. Happy to draft a short appendix that lists what constitutes acceptable evidence.

— Dev
Principal Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Gray <oliver.gray@neptune.com>, Katy Simmons <katy.simmons@neptune.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-09T13:20:00Z
Subject: RE: Neptune redlines on MSA (liability section)

Oliver / Katy — thanks for the initial redlines. Laura and Dev provided feedback and we've drafted the counterproposal (attached) that: (a) accepts an uncapped carve-out for proven fraud and intentional wrongdoing (subject to clear-and-convincing proof), (b) narrows "willful misconduct" language to intentional acts only, (c) treats reckless conduct separately with a monetary floor ($500k) or demonstrable data impact, and (d) sets our aggregate cap at the greater of $6M or 2x prior 12 months' fees (excluding uncapped categories).

We also included an evidence appendix listing the logs and artifacts we'll produce to support intent findings. Please review the tracked redline (attachment) and let's set a 30-minute call tomorrow to resolve any open points. If we can settle definitions, we can fast-follow caps in a second pass.

Attachment: Redwood_Counter_Neptune_MSA_20261009.docx (redline)

Best,
Jonas

From: Katy Simmons <katy.simmons@neptune.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Oliver Gray <oliver.gray@neptune.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-11T16:45:00Z
Subject: RE: Liability redlines: materiality and fraud/gross-negligence thresholds (Neptune)

Jonas / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the detailed counter. We appreciate the evidence appendix and the move to tighten definitions. A few notes from our side before the call:
- We can accept the narrowed definition of willful misconduct but need to preserve a path for uncapped recovery for egregious data-exfiltration events even if intent is difficult to prove up front.
- On the reckless carve-out, the $500k floor is reasonable, but request an exception where customer personal data is involved (lower floor of $250k where PII is compromised).
- Regarding the aggregate cap: Neptune prefers a higher dollar floor for strategic procurements. Can you confirm whether the $6M floor is negotiable for enterprise accounts?

Let's take these brief items on the call. Can you do 2026-10-12 10:00am PT?

Katy
VP, Procurement, Neptune Analytics
